title: Build a BFS shortest-path finder in Go
description: Greenfield Go task: implement ShortestPath using BFS on an unweighted adjacency list, returning the path as a slice or nil if unreachable.

task_spec.prompt:
Implement ShortestPath in internal/bfs/bfs.go.

package bfs

// ShortestPath returns the shortest path from start to end in the unweighted
// directed graph represented as an adjacency list. Returns nil if end is
// unreachable from start. Returns []int{start} if start == end.
func ShortestPath(graph map[int][]int, start, end int) []int

Algorithm:
1. If start == end, return []int{start}.
2. BFS: maintain a visited set and a parent map.
3. When end is found, reconstruct the path by following parent pointers back to start, then reverse.
4. Return nil if end not found.

All 5 tests in internal/bfs/bfs_test.go must pass.
Run: go test ./...
required_artifacts: BFS explores nodes level by level
Parent map is used to reconstruct the path
Returns nil when end is unreachable
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `go test ./...` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
